queries.note: present with no value reads as the empty string, not absent
an empty value reads as the empty string, not absent
the first pair wins on a duplicate key
keys are percent-decoded before comparison, so an encoded spelling is the same key and competes for first place
`+` is a space in the value; `%20` decodes too
other keys are ignored, in either position
an escaped `%` decodes to a literal `%`, never read as a second escape
a `%` not followed by two hex digits refuses the query rather than reading as text
a trailing bare `%` refuses the query
decoded bytes that are not UTF-8 refuse the query rather than reading as U+FFFD
an undecodable escape in a key no reader reads still refuses the whole query, wherever it sits
an undecodable key refuses the query too
